Aalberts.why: its semicon segment (21% of revenue) builds modules for semiconductor equipment, mostly lithography systems, and is growing on AI-driven fab demand with a new Dronten factory
Aalberts.evidence: Aalberts Q2 FY2026 call (07-23-2026): CEO - Dronten factory ramp-up in 2027 'mostly for lithography systems'; semicon Q2 organic growth 16%, strong front-end and back-end

players.product: semiconductor-equipment modules and mechatronic subsystems, mostly for lithography systems (front-end), plus back-end equipment parts and wafer-handling pre-aligners (semicon segment)

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: revenue EUR 1.5 billion with 5% organic growth; EBITA EUR 225 million, 14.4% of revenue; net profit EUR 158 million; EPS EUR 1.47 (+EUR 0.09); free cash flow EUR 89 million; added value margin 65.5%; debt/EBITDA 1.9. Semicon now represents 21% of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue EUR 1.5 billion (organic +5%); EBITA EUR 225 million (14.4%); EPS EUR 1.47

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook confirmed: FY2026 improved organic growth and EBITA margin versus 2025; capex guidance around EUR 190 million (H1: EUR 71 million, H2 step-up for Dronten). CEO: semicon organic growth in H2 2026 expected similar to Q2, 'a bit more than 16%', and for 2027 similar, with GVT added to organic growth from Q4 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: capex EUR 190 million; semicon H2 organic growth a bit more than 16%

quarterly_data.signal: Semicon segment: Q2 2026 organic growth of 16%, higher than expected (growth had been expected in H2), with strong demand in both front-end and back-end driven by AI adoption and a very healthy order book; GVT (acquired at a revenue level of EUR 107 million) contributes positively to growth and margins. CEO: Aalberts aims to become more and more an integrated module provider for front-end and back-end customers; no further semicon acquisition expected in 2026.

Capacity (CEO): the greenfield factory in Dronten, Netherlands is in its final step, with ramp-up in 2027 mostly for lithography systems; capacity is being added in Penang, Malaysia for back-end customers. 'Our biggest customer, I've made it public, they expect 30% growth this year' and asks suppliers to be ready for 30%; customers are sending capacity requests without orders; the capacity plan is aligned with that demand. CFO: assets under construction way over EUR 200 million, mostly Dronten, with depreciation of around EUR 6 million for the site.
quarterly_data.figure: customer expects 30% growth; Dronten depreciation around EUR 6 million

quarterly_data.signal: Data centers (Building segment): roughly 2% of Building revenue with an addressable market of EUR 1.5 billion and double-digit organic growth, especially in North America; the order book increases month after month with flow control and boiler-room technologies, prefab solutions, connection and piping systems for primary and secondary cooling loops (e.g. stainless-steel air separators and ball valves of own design).
quarterly_data.figure: addressable market EUR 1.5 billion; about 2% of Building revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Other segments, H1 2026: Building organic growth 2.9% with 13.5% EBITA margin (no shipments to the Middle East in Q2, weak European residential connection systems); Industry organic growth 6.4% with 18.6% EBITA margin, driven by aerospace, power generation and defense.
